BiblicalUsage: The word names a fountain or spring, and it appears at the end of life and in the promise of restoration. The Preacher says the pitcher is broken at the fountain and the wheel broken at the cistern, and Isaiah says the parched ground shall become a pool and the thirsty land springs of water, and the Shepherd shall lead His people by the springs of water.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the fountain is broken at death and opened again in the promise, because God gives water to the thirsty land. I hold that He who leads His people by springs of water will not let them thirst forever.
